questions.sub_skill: Interpret an Azure Resource Manager template or a Bicep file
questions.prompt: An ARM template has a parameter location with defaultValue "[resourceGroup().location]". You deploy it to resource group RG1 in West Europe without passing location. Where are the resources created?
options: The region of the subscription's first resource group
West Europe, the location of RG1
The deployment fails because location is required
The region of the machine running the deployment
questions.explanation: resourceGroup().location returns the location of the resource group being deployed to, so the default resolves to West Europe.
why_not: There's no such rule; the function reads the target resource group.
It has a default value, so it isn't required.
The client's location plays no part.
questions.clue: "defaultValue [resourceGroup().location]" and no value passed: the default comes from the target resource group.

questions.sub_skill: Interpret an Azure Resource Manager template or a Bicep file
questions.prompt: A Bicep file defines var storageName = 'st${uniqueString(resourceGroup().id)}'. You deploy it twice to the same resource group. What happens to the storage account name?
options: It's identical both times, so the second deployment updates the same account
It changes each time, creating a second account
The second deployment fails because the name is taken
It's random but guaranteed unique across Azure
questions.explanation: uniqueString() returns the same hash for the same input, giving a name that is unique per resource group and repeatable.
why_not: uniqueString is deterministic: the same input returns the same value.
It's the same resource in the same group, so it's an update, not a conflict.
It isn't random; it's a hash of the input.
questions.clue: "uniqueString(resourceGroup().id)" deployed "twice to the same resource group": the same input gives the same name.

questions.sub_skill: Interpret an Azure Resource Manager template or a Bicep file
questions.prompt: In a Bicep file, resource vnet '...' = {...} is followed by resource nic '...' = { properties: { ipConfigurations: [ { properties: { subnet: { id: vnet.properties.subnets[0].id } } } ] } }. There's no dependsOn. In what order are they deployed?
options: In parallel, because there's no dependsOn
The NIC first, because it appears later in the file
The VNet first, then the NIC, because referencing vnet by its symbolic name creates an implicit dependency
The deployment fails until you add dependsOn
questions.explanation: Referencing another resource by symbolic name, including through parent, makes Bicep generate the dependsOn in the compiled template.
why_not: Bicep adds dependsOn automatically when one resource references another's symbolic name.
File order doesn't determine deployment order.
Bicep infers the dependency; explicit dependsOn isn't needed.
questions.clue: "There's no dependsOn" but the NIC references vnet by its symbolic name: Bicep infers the order.

questions.sub_skill: Modify an existing Azure Resource Manager template
questions.prompt: You add a blob container resource to an ARM template that already deploys its storage account. Deployments sometimes fail because the parent account isn't found. What should you add to the container resource?
options: A condition property
A copy loop
An output referencing the storage account
A dependsOn entry with the storage account's resourceId()
questions.explanation: Without dependsOn, resources deploy in parallel. dependsOn makes Resource Manager finish the account before the container.
why_not: Conditions decide whether a resource deploys, not when.
Copy loops create multiple instances; they don't order deployment.
Outputs don't affect deployment order.
questions.clue: "parent account isn't found" sometimes: ARM JSON needs an explicit dependsOn.

questions.sub_skill: Modify an existing Azure Resource Manager template
questions.prompt: An ARM template's skuName parameter has allowedValues ["Standard_LRS", "Standard_GRS"]. A team must deploy with Standard_ZRS. What's the minimal change?
options: Change defaultValue to Standard_ZRS
Add "Standard_ZRS" to the parameter's allowedValues
Remove the parameter and hard-code the SKU
Add Standard_ZRS to the parameters file
questions.explanation: allowedValues restricts accepted values. Add the new value to the list.
why_not: The default must still be an allowed value, and passing ZRS would still be rejected.
That removes flexibility; it isn't the minimal change.
Parameter values outside allowedValues are rejected at deployment.
questions.clue: "allowedValues" excludes the value the team needs: add it to the list.

questions.sub_skill: Modify an existing Azure Resource Manager template
questions.prompt: An ARM template takes an adminPassword parameter of type string. Security finds the password visible in the deployment history. What should you change?
options: Change the parameter type to securestring
Move the password into a variable
Output the password instead
Deploy in complete mode
questions.explanation: securestring and secureobject values aren't saved to the deployment history or logged.
why_not: Variables are stored in the template and are no more secret.
Outputs are recorded in deployment history.
Deployment mode doesn't affect what's logged.
questions.clue: "password visible in the deployment history": the parameter type must be securestring.

questions.prompt: In a Bicep file you must ensure deployers can only pass 'Standard_LRS' or 'Standard_ZRS' for param skuName string. What do you add?
options: An @secure() decorator
An if condition on the resource
An @allowed(['Standard_LRS', 'Standard_ZRS']) decorator above the parameter
A @description decorator listing the values
questions.explanation: @allowed restricts a parameter to a list of values, like allowedValues in ARM JSON.
why_not: @secure hides the value; it doesn't restrict it.
A condition controls whether the resource deploys, not which values are allowed.
A description documents; it doesn't enforce anything.
questions.clue: "can only pass" two values in Bicep: the @allowed decorator.

questions.prompt: You need to add a blob container to an existing Bicep file that declares resource stg 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts@2023-05-01'. Which approach needs no explicit dependsOn?
options: Declare the container with name: 'stg/default/reports' and no parent
Declare the container as an existing resource
Add the container as an output
Declare a blobServices resource with parent: stg, then the container with parent pointing to it
questions.explanation: parent references the parent by symbolic name, so Bicep generates the dependencies automatically.
why_not: The slash-name form needs an explicit dependsOn to guarantee ordering.
existing references something already deployed; it doesn't create it.
Outputs return values; they don't deploy resources.
questions.clue: "needs no explicit dependsOn" for a child resource: declare it with parent.

questions.prompt: A Bicep file must reference a Log Analytics workspace that another team already deployed, to read its ID, without redeploying it. What should you declare?
options: A resource with the existing keyword and the workspace's name
A module pointing at the other team's file
A new resource with the same name
A param containing the workspace object
questions.explanation: The existing keyword declares a reference to a resource that already exists; it isn't deployed or modified.
why_not: That would deploy their resources as part of your deployment.
That would redeploy, and potentially reconfigure, their workspace.
Parameters pass values in; they don't read a resource's current properties.
questions.clue: "another team already deployed" and "without redeploying it": the existing keyword.

questions.sub_skill: Deploy resources by using an Azure Resource Manager template or a Bicep file
questions.prompt: A resource group contains VM1, VNet1 and storage1. You deploy a template defining only storage1, using complete mode. What happens?
options: Nothing happens to VM1 and VNet1
VM1 and VNet1 are deleted, because they aren't in the template
The deployment fails because the template is incomplete
VM1 and VNet1 are moved to a new resource group
questions.explanation: In complete mode, Resource Manager deletes resources in the resource group that aren't in the template. What-if first, or use incremental mode.
why_not: That describes incremental mode.
Complete mode deploys; it deletes what's missing.
Deployments never move resources.
questions.clue: "complete mode" with a template that defines only storage1: anything else in the group is deleted.

questions.sub_skill: Deploy resources by using an Azure Resource Manager template or a Bicep file
questions.prompt: Before deploying a changed Bicep file to production, you must see exactly which resources would be created, modified or deleted, without changing anything. What should you run?
options: az bicep build
az deployment group validate
az deployment group what-if (or New-AzResourceGroupDeployment -WhatIf)
az group export
questions.explanation: The what-if operation predicts Create, Delete, Modify, NoChange and other changes without deploying.
why_not: build only compiles the file to JSON; it doesn't compare with Azure.
Validation checks the template is deployable; it doesn't list per-resource changes.
Export produces a template from current resources; it doesn't preview changes.
questions.clue: "see exactly which resources would be created, modified or deleted, without changing anything": what-if.

questions.sub_skill: Deploy resources by using an Azure Resource Manager template or a Bicep file
questions.prompt: You use one Bicep file for dev and prod, with different SKU and instance counts. What is the intended way to supply the values?
options: A parameters file per environment, such as dev.bicepparam and prod.bicepparam
Two copies of the Bicep file with hard-coded values
Variables with both sets of values and complete mode
Outputs that switch the values
questions.explanation: Parameters files, JSON or .bicepparam, supply per-environment values to the same template.
why_not: That duplicates the template and invites drift.
Mode doesn't select values; parameters do.
Outputs return values; they don't feed inputs.
questions.clue: "one Bicep file for dev and prod" with different values: one parameters file per environment.

questions.sub_skill: Export a deployment as an Azure Resource Manager template or convert an Azure Resource Manager template to a Bicep file
questions.prompt: Resources were created manually in the portal. You need a Bicep file describing them as a starting point, and you only have the Azure CLI and the portal. What's the most direct way?
options: az group export --output bicep
Copy the template from the resource group's deployment history
bicep build on the resource group
Portal: the resource group > Export template > Bicep
questions.explanation: Bicep files can currently be exported only from the portal. With the CLI, export JSON and then decompile it.
why_not: The CLI exports ARM JSON; Bicep export is portal-only.
Manually created resources may have no deployment entry, and history gives JSON.
build compiles Bicep you already have; it doesn't read Azure.
questions.clue: "created manually in the portal" and you need Bicep: export the resource group template as Bicep.

questions.sub_skill: Export a deployment as an Azure Resource Manager template or convert an Azure Resource Manager template to a Bicep file
questions.prompt: An auditor needs the exact template that was used by a deployment last Tuesday, not the resources' current state. Where do you get it?
options: Export template on the resource group
The resource group's Deployments page: select the deployment and open its template
Decompile the current resources
The Activity log's JSON for the storage account
questions.explanation: Deployment history keeps a copy of the template each deployment used (ARM JSON).
why_not: Export reflects current resources and is reconstructed, not the template that was used.
Decompile converts JSON to Bicep; it doesn't retrieve history.
The activity log records operations, not the template.
questions.clue: "exact template used by a deployment last Tuesday", not current state: the deployment history.

questions.sub_skill: Export a deployment as an Azure Resource Manager template or convert an Azure Resource Manager template to a Bicep file
questions.prompt: You decompile a large ARM template with bicep decompile. The Bicep file builds but has linter warnings and an unusual symbolic name. What's true?
options: Decompilation is best-effort; the output is functionally equivalent but may need cleanup
The decompiler has failed and the Bicep file won't deploy
You must redeploy the original JSON to fix the Bicep file
JSON → Bicep → JSON returns the byte-identical original
questions.explanation: Microsoft describes decompile as best-effort with no guaranteed mapping. You may need to fix warnings and rename symbols.
why_not: Warnings don't stop deployment; the output is functionally equivalent.
The fix is to edit the Bicep file.
Round trips produce functionally equivalent, not identical, templates.
questions.clue: "decompile" with warnings: decompilation is best-effort and needs review.
